stories.author: Judd Legum
stories.title: UPDATE: ICE is leaving hospitals with millions in unpaid bills
stories.text: An exterior view of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) abruptly stopping paying third parties for medical care provided to detainees. Third-party providers are used to provide “medically necessary” care including “dialysis, prenatal care, oncology, [and] chemotherapy,” according to ICE. Prior to that date, payment for medical care for ICE detainees was processed by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). But the VA “ abruptly and instantly terminated ” its agreement with ICE after the arrangement, which dated to the George W. Bush administration, drew criticism from right-wing activists. The activists falsely claimed that undocumented immigrants were siphoning resources from veterans. Actually, ICE was fully reimbursing the VA for the service. According to documents published by ICE on a government contracting website on November 12, 2025, the termination of the agreement with the VA left ICE unable to “pay for medically necessary off-site care.” ICE described this as an “absolute emergency” that needed to be resolved “immediately” to “prevent any further medical complications or loss of life.” Eleven months later, ICE still has no system to pay for outside medical car

stories.title: ICE’s Robot Dogs; WNBA Does Counter-terror; Flock and Awe
stories.text: Boston Dynamics’ robot dog — coming to an ICE field office near you Three bizarre stories caught my eye this weekend, all insane and all pointing to the same thing: national security's war on American daily life. Flock cameras . The AI-fueled license plate reading network is conquering America at an alarming pace, having found an ingenious end-run around our right to privacy: selling to the neighbors instead of the cops. ICE is acquiring robot dogs. The most hated agency in America is shopping for Boston Dynamics quadrupeds to take another bite out of the quaint notion that this country isn’t a battlefield. WNBA embraces Counterterrorism. The league is in the news this month not for its playoffs but for hiring a threat intelligence firm — one built to fight ISIS — to handle a supposed "extremist" menace to its players. National security has colonized American culture so completely that none of this registers as creepy. Flock cameras become a cranky privacy controversy. ICE’s robo-dogs become a zany story you roll your eyes at. A counterterrorism firm for basketball players becomes a friendly write-up on NPR about the importance of combating extremism in sports. stories.title: A Graham Platner Write-In Campaign Might End Up Helping Troy Jackson
stories.text: A bubbling effort by a small group of Graham Platner’s supporters in Maine to write the former Senate candidate’s name on the ballot in November has begun to attract online attention, as Cheyenne Hunt, the Democratic operative who crusaded against Platner, has publicly denounced the possibility. “Platner supporters are posting in a private Facebook group, reporting back on their conversations with him. Allegedly, Platner himself has ‘endorsed’ the write-in strategy laid out here,” Hunt wrote . “This final act of hubris and selfishness would only help Collins win in November.” Collins is of course Sen. Susan Collins, who Democratic nominee Troy Jackson will face in November. Jackson replaced Platner on the ballot after Platner dropped out in July following a rape allegation that was brought to Politico and CNN by Hunt . Drop Site is always free to read. One of the organizers of the campaign to write in Platner’s name, Scott Niemi, published an oped about it in the Bangor Daily News; a Portland Press-Herald columnist has denounced the effort ; and a New York Post reporter has reached out to the people involved.
